title: Availability Zones: physical isolation within a Region
hook: Availability Zones (AZs) are separate data centers within one Region, connected by low-latency networking. Spreading production tiers across at least two AZs survives the loss of a single building or power domain.

blocks.text: Each Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and networking. AZ names like ap-south-1a and ap-south-1b are labels within a Region — they are not guaranteed to map the same physical layout in another Region. High availability designs place redundant capacity in multiple AZs: Application Load Balancer targets in two subnets, RDS Multi-AZ standby in another AZ, Auto Scaling groups balanced across AZs.

entries.plainDefinition: Isolated data center group inside a Region.
entries.example: ap-south-1a and ap-south-1b host redundant app tiers.

entries.plainDefinition: Resources replicated or standby across AZs for fault tolerance.
entries.example: RDS Multi-AZ synchronous standby in another AZ.

entries.plainDefinition: Stable identifier for an AZ across accounts (use-az1).
entries.example: Map consistent AZ IDs when pairing DR accounts.

entries.plainDefinition: Data transfer between AZs in the same Region — billed per GB.
entries.example: Replica traffic between app tiers in different AZs.

blocks.text: Single-AZ deployments fail when one data center has an outage — a real event, not a theoretical edge case. Interviewers expect you to name which tiers are multi-AZ and which are intentionally single-AZ with tradeoffs.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: AZ failure is a design input. Stateless app tier across AZs; stateful tier uses Multi-AZ or cross-AZ replication with eyes open on latency and cost.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Subnet per AZ
items.body: Create one subnet per AZ in your VPC. Never stretch one subnet across AZs.

items.title: Spread compute
items.body: Auto Scaling or Elastic Container Service (ECS)/Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) spread tasks across AZ subnets.

items.title: Load balance
items.body: Application Load Balancer listens in multiple AZ public subnets.

items.title: Protect data
items.body: RDS Multi-AZ, ElastiCache replication, or application-level quorum across AZs.

snippet.label: List AZs in a Region
snippet.explanation: Verify three or more AZs before designing triple-AZ layout. State must be available.

snippet.label: Auto Scaling across AZs
snippet.code:
AppAutoScalingGroup:
  Type: AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup
  Properties:
    VPCZoneIdentifier:
      - !Ref PublicSubnetAzA
      - !Ref PublicSubnetAzB
    MinSize: "2"
    MaxSize: "6"
    DesiredCapacity: "4"
    HealthCheckType: ELB
    TargetGroupARNs:
      - !Ref AppTargetGroup
snippet.explanation: VPCZoneIdentifier pins instances to subnets in distinct AZs. Combined with ALB, losing one AZ drops capacity but service stays up.

snippet.label: RDS Multi-AZ status
snippet.explanation: MultiAZ true confirms synchronous standby in another AZ. Read replicas are a separate HA/scale mechanism.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Running production RDS single-AZ to save money. One NAT Gateway serving all AZs — AZ outage kills egress for everyone. Assuming ap-south-1a in two accounts is the same physical AZ without checking AZ IDs.

interviewTakeaways: AZs are isolated data centers within a Region — design for at least two AZs for production.
Subnets are AZ-scoped; spread ALB, compute, and Multi-AZ data tiers accordingly.
Cross-AZ traffic costs money — still cheaper than downtime from single-AZ.
60s: Multi-AZ = survive one data center loss. Subnet per AZ. RDS Multi-AZ and ALB across AZs. Not the same as multi-Region.
Follow-up: difference between RDS Multi-AZ and read replica?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'we are HA because we use AWS' without naming AZ spread gets you rejected.
Strong answer: list tiers, which are multi-AZ, and what fails when one AZ dies.
Single NAT Gateway for the whole VPC — AZ failure becomes company-wide egress outage.
Treating read replica as Multi-AZ failover without promotion runbook.

jsTsCorrelations.note: PM2 cluster on one VM is not multi-AZ. ECS/Fargate spread across AZ subnets matches how you would run multiple Kestrel instances behind a load balancer on-prem.
ALB deregisters unhealthy targets per AZ during outage — similar to taking an IIS server out of Application Request Routing rotation in a C# farm without redeploying code.
